text: The Prime Minister accepted your resignation in month {months}. The Army you handed on is smaller than the one you were given, and the junior leaders who should have been holding it together are not where they should be: what was raised was led by whoever was nearest. Your successor has been told to start with the leadership figures.
oneLiner: Resigned in month {months}. The corporals ran out before the soldiers did.

text: The Prime Minister accepted your resignation in month {months}. Force Ready stood at {ese} against a target of {target}, from {headcount} personnel. Your successor has taken the programme on, and has read your notes. The verdict on the mobilisation is deferred; the verdict on the minister is not.
oneLiner: Resigned in month {months} with {ese} of {target} ready.

text: You delivered {headcount} personnel and {ese} soldiers' worth of them, against a target of {target}. The formation is led, equipped and largely regular or reservist, and its junior leaders are where they should be. It cost the Treasury about £{costBn}bn and the economy about £{gdpLossBn}bn in lost output. Nobody will remember either figure. The general's note is one line: it will do.
oneLiner: Target met with a force that is actually a force. It will do.

text: You delivered {headcount} personnel and {ese} soldiers' worth of them against a target of {target}, clearing it by {surplus}. Almost all of them were soldiers already on the day you took office: the call-out and the recall did the work, and anything the training pipeline added arrived as margin rather than as the answer. The general's note is appreciative and short. It observes that a force this size can be found without building anything, and that the next one up cannot.
oneLiner: Target met with {surplus} to spare. A force this size can be found, not built.

text: Target met: {ese} against {target}, from {headcount} personnel. The quality is good and the leadership is stretched; the junior NCOs have been doing two jobs for {months} months and it shows in the sickness returns. The general's advice is to deploy now, before the corporals notice that they can leave. Cost to the Treasury: about £{costBn}bn.
oneLiner: Target met. Good soldiers, tired corporals.

text: You delivered {headcount} personnel counting as {ese} soldiers, over a target of {target}. The return reads {regulars} regulars, {reservists} reservists of one kind or another and {conscripts} conscripts, and the parts of it have not yet learned to trust each other. The general calls it a division that will improve with contact and hopes the enemy allows the time. The bill was about £{costBn}bn.
oneLiner: Target met, mid quality: a division that needs a quiet first month.

text: You fielded {ese} soldiers against a target of {target}: {shortfall} short. What you fielded is good: regulars, reservists and a leadership cadre that is still intact. The general told the ally he would rather have this than the number. The ally wanted the number. The Treasury cost was about £{costBn}bn.
oneLiner: {shortfall} short, but what exists is real.

text: Against a target of {target} you fielded {ese}: a shortfall of {shortfall}, after {months} months. What exists is in good order, and it is in good order partly because there is less of it: an establishment that is not stretched does not show the strain. The general's assessment spends one paragraph on the quality and the rest on the gap. The ally has been told the number, and has not asked for the quality figures.
oneLiner: {shortfall} short, and good order was never the thing in question.

text: Target missed by {shortfall}, and the leadership figures are worse than the headline. The corporals who should have been leading sections are running the training estate instead: the schools built to raise the force took the people the force needed to be led by. Hand them back and the cadre holds, which is the part that will be difficult to explain. The regular Army you inherited has been hollowed to supply a force that did not arrive.
oneLiner: Missed by {shortfall}. The corporals went to the schools; no division came out.

text: Target missed by {shortfall}, and the leadership figures are worse than the headline. You called up {conscripts} conscripts, which is more than the Army has corporals and sergeants to put in front of them: recalling every instructor from every training school would not have closed the gap. What arrived was a crowd with a chain of command drawn on it. The general's note runs to a page; the first sentence is the one that will be quoted.
oneLiner: Missed by {shortfall}. You raised more soldiers than the Army had corporals.

text: You fielded {headcount} people who count as {ese} soldiers, {shortfall} short of the target. The holding pools, the unequipped graduates and the untraced reservists all appear in the ledger and none of them appears in the line. The general observes that about £{costBn}bn has been converted into headcount without passing through capability. He does not say whose fault that is.
oneLiner: {headcount} on the books, {ese} in the line. Missed by {shortfall}.

text: Target missed: {ese} against {target}, a shortfall of {shortfall} after {months} months. The force that exists is respectable. In another six months it would have been a division. Every minister in this position has wanted to write that sentence. The ally has been told. The general has asked that the pipeline be kept running regardless.
oneLiner: Missed by {shortfall}. Six more months and it would have been a division.

text: The deadline has passed. Force Ready stood at {ese} against a target of {target}, from {headcount} personnel, at a Treasury cost of about £{costBn}bn. The general has submitted his assessment through the proper channels. It is being considered.
oneLiner: {ese} ready of {target}. The assessment is being considered.
